question: How does a single artificial neuron compute its output?

storyboard.learning_goal: Understand that a single neuron computes output y = f(w·x + b): scale each input by its weight, add them plus a bias, then apply a non-linear activation to decide output magnitude.
storyboard.driving_question: How does a single artificial neuron turn several input numbers into one output number?
storyboard.learner_start: Knows basic arithmetic (multiply, add) and idea of a function mapping input to output; no prior knowledge of weights or activations.
storyboard.concrete_example: One trackable neuron with 2 inputs: x1=0.9, x2=0.2, weights w1=0.6, w2=-1.2, bias b=0.1, sigmoid activation -> z=0.40, y~0.60
storyboard.representation: Chosen method: worked symbolic execution + geometric construction (Math 01 style). Why it fits: learning goal is a mechanism y=f(sum+b) where changing notation must expose structure; we build the equation alongside a persistent neuron diagram so each term has a visible referent and consequence. Capability gap: renderer limited to circle, box, text, arrow, line, path, svg, so activation curve is drawn as svg path with sampled points, not native Manim plot; sufficient for this 2-input case.

visual_design.why: The relationship is a mechanism with symbolic structure: parallel scaling then summation then thresholding. A central neuron diagram preserves identity while side equations expose the quantitative transform.
visual_design.misreading: Thicker line or bigger input might be read as larger output alone, ignoring sign and bias/activation
visual_design.safeguard: Keep numeric labels w=+0.6, w=-1.2 on lines with +/- colors in legend, keep product values and sum equation visible, and show bias as separate additive arrow into sum box
encodings: position: left inputs -> center neuron -> right output shows flow direction
line thickness/color: weight lines thicker/brighter for larger magnitude; blue positive, orange negative
box fill/number: sum accumulator shows numeric total
curve + moving dot: activation path maps sum value on x-axis to output on y-axis

beats.question: What does the neuron do to each input individually?
beats.insight: Each input is scaled by its own weight; sign flips or suppresses influence.
beats.before: Empty stage with question. No neuron yet.
beats.change: Two input circles appear left with values x1=0.9, x2=0.2; center neuron circle appears; connecting lines grow with labels w1=+0.6 (blue thick) and w2=-1.2 (orange thick); product chips p1=0.54, p2=-0.24 appear on lines.
beats.after: Viewer sees 2 inputs, 2 weighted edges, and computed products: 0.9*0.6=0.54 and 0.2*-1.2=-0.24, feeding toward center.
beats.reasoning: Visible scaling from line thickness plus explicit product makes weight-as-volume-knob inference possible; sign color prevents magnitude-only reading.
beats.camera: Static wide on inputs-to-center so both scalings comparable.
beats.narration: A neuron doesn't see raw inputs. It multiplies each one by a weight it learned. A positive weight passes it through, a negative weight flips it against the decision.
beats.visual_test: Viewer can point to each line and state its product and whether it votes for or against the output.

beats.question: How are those separate votes combined into one drive?
beats.insight: Weighted votes add together plus a bias that shifts the total up or down independent of inputs.
beats.before: Inputs, weight lines, and products from b1 remain.
beats.change: Sum box appears inside/adjacent to neuron, products slide into it as 0.54 + (-0.24); bias arrow labeled b=+0.1 enters from below; total updates to z=0.40 shown large.
beats.after: Viewer sees accumulator equation z=0.54-0.24+0.1=0.40 as single drive value entering activation stage.
beats.reasoning: Animating products converging into one box plus separate bias arrow makes additivity and bias-as-shift visible, not just a formula.
beats.camera: Push to center sum box to read addition while keeping inputs in frame for orientation.
beats.narration: Now it adds those votes together, and adds one extra number called bias. Bias shifts the total even when inputs are silent, like presetting how easily this neuron fires.
beats.visual_test: Viewer can explain why z is 0.4 not 0.3, naming the bias contribution.

beats.question: Why not output that sum directly?
beats.insight: Activation squashes the unbounded sum into a bounded decision value; small sum changes near threshold matter most.
beats.before: Sum value z=0.40 held in center with inputs and weights dimmed but present.
beats.change: Sigmoid curve svg appears right of neuron with x=z, y=output axes; dot travels along curve to x=0.40, y rises to ~0.60; linear dashed line shown then faded to contrast unbounded growth vs squashed 0-1 range.
beats.after: Viewer sees z=0.40 mapped to y~0.60 on 0-1 curve, understanding activation as squash/threshold, not just another multiply.
beats.reasoning: Contrasting unbounded line vs saturating curve and landing dot at 0.6 makes non-linearity a geometric necessity for bounded decisions.
beats.camera: Pan right to activation curve, keep z=0.40 connector line linking center to curve x-position.
beats.narration: If we output the sum, one large input could explode it. The neuron squeezes it through a squishy function. Around zero a small push changes the answer a lot, far away it saturates.
beats.visual_test: Viewer can show where z=0.4 lands on curve and predict that larger z saturates near 1, not grows forever.

beats.question: So what is the complete computation end-to-end?
beats.insight: Full forward pass is one pipeline: products -> sum+bias -> activation, yielding a single usable output that changes predictably if weight or input changes.
beats.before: Full chain visible: inputs left, sum center, curve right with output 0.60.
beats.change: Output circle appears far right with y=0.60; full equation y=sigmoid(0.9*0.6+0.2*-1.2+0.1) lights in sequence left-to-right; then x1 pulses from 0.9 to 0.1 showing output dropping to ~0.42 to prove causality.
beats.after: Viewer sees entire pipeline animated in order and sees output respond to input change, generalizing the rule y=f(w.x+b).
beats.reasoning: Replaying the same example end-to-end with sequential highlight plus a counterfactual input change proves the pipeline causes the output, not just labels flowing.
beats.camera: Pull back to full left-to-right pipeline for comparison, then focus on output value.
beats.narration: So the whole neuron is this: scale, add and shift, then squish. With our numbers we get about point six. Drop the spam word and the same neuron drops its vote. That pipeline is all a neuron ever does.
beats.interaction: Drag x1 slider 0.9 to 0.1 and predict new output before reveal
beats.visual_test: Viewer can recite steps with numbers and predict direction of output change when an input or weight increases.

Push to center sum box while keeping inputs in frame
Pan right to activation curve keeping z connector linked
Pull back to full left-to-right pipeline then focus output

answer: A neuron computes y = f(sum_i w_i*x_i + b): multiply each input x_i by its weight w_i, sum all products, add bias b to get logit z, then apply activation f (e.g., sigmoid, ReLU) to get y. Example: z=0.9*0.6+0.2*(-1.2)+0.1=0.40, y=sigmoid(0.40)~0.60.
